blockchain.heroSubtitle: An immutable source of truth for KYC, Vehicle Inspection (e-Check), Digital License and every legally auditable ATTT process.
blockchain.howTitle: How does the new layer work?
blockchain.howDesc: Every institutional event (a ticket, a payment, an inspection, a license issuance) becomes a digitally signed transaction that travels through a permissioned blockchain network before being considered official.
blockchain.step1Desc: SERTRACEN, SIGED, 3Tech e-Car Check, Courts and DNOT Impound Yards generate a digital event with the citizen's identity and the official timestamp.
blockchain.step2Desc: The event is signed with the issuing entity's cryptographic key and reduced to a unique, unrepeatable SHA-256 hash.
blockchain.step3Desc: Authorized nodes (ATTT, SERTRACEN, Electoral Tribunal, insurers, banks) validate the transaction through the network's consensus protocol.
blockchain.step4Desc: The transaction is grouped into a block cryptographically linked to the previous one, forming a continuous, tamper-proof chain.
blockchain.step5Desc: The record becomes available for audit, judicial forensics or public verification, with no possibility of retroactive alteration.
blockchain.networkDesc: 3D visualization of the permissioned network: each node represents an entity that validates and shares the same distributed ledger.
blockchain.fabricDesc: Enterprise permissioned blockchain framework (Linux Foundation), ideal for government consortiums that require identity control, private channels and high throughput without gas costs.
blockchain.fabricFeature1: Identity managed by an MSP (Membership Service Provider) — each institution keeps its own certificate authority.
blockchain.fabricFeature2: Private channels: ATTT can share sensitive KYC data only with the Electoral Tribunal or the relevant insurer.
blockchain.fabricFeature3: Chaincode (smart contracts) in Go, Java or TypeScript to automate license, policy and contempt validations.
blockchain.fabricFeature4: High throughput (thousands of tx/sec) with no transaction fees, suitable for national volume.
blockchain.altDesc: Hyperledger Fabric is the main recommendation, but these alternatives are also viable depending on the use case.
blockchain.useCasesTitle: Use Cases on the same network
blockchain.useCasesDesc: The blockchain layer isn't just for the audit log — it certifies citizen identity, vehicles and credentials.
blockchain.kycDesc: The citizen's verified identity (national ID, Electoral Tribunal biometrics, driving record) is anchored to the network via a hash, letting SERTRACEN, banks and insurers confirm identity without duplicating processes.
blockchain.echeckDesc: Every 82-point inspection certificate is recorded as a transaction signed by the certified workshop and ATTT, creating an unalterable vehicle history available for policies and transfers.
blockchain.licenseDesc: The driver's license and clearance certificate are issued as verifiable credentials anchored to the blockchain, downloadable directly to Apple Wallet and Google Wallet for offline verification at any checkpoint.
blockchain.walletTitle: Add to Apple Wallet / Google Wallet
blockchain.walletDesc: The digital document contains a signed QR code and a public verification link. A traffic officer can validate authenticity even offline, comparing the local hash against the network's latest sync.
blockchain.chainDesc: Every block references the hash of the previous one. Altering a single record would break the entire chain — that's why it's the legal source of truth.
blockchain.ctaDesc: This layer integrates with the existing Audit Log module, offering legal traceability to judges, insurers and citizens themselves.
